title: FP64 K reduction is a promising C550 FP8 accuracy route but has no Cake vocabulary or formal Workload qualification
observation: A standalone one-row Triton source decodes E4M3FN inputs to FP32, forms FP32 products, reduces K in FP64 and rounds the result to FP32. It compiled to native xcore1000 mcfatbin on C550-1 Triton 3.1 and C550-2 Triton 3.6. C550-2 broker job maca-d52933c85e85 matched all 20480 words of the original five frozen outputs plus 4096 words from the first plain-sum held-out failure matrix bitwise, with unchanged FP8 input bytes. A first same-source 10-pair MCPTI run retained all raw activity but failed the predeclared maximum CV 0.05 in one candidate cohort (0.052775); it is not a valid speedup. A fresh create-only successor, job maca-fa47df57195d, passed the quality gate, 10/10 pair wins and A/A close_null: the FP64 candidate and one-row compensated baseline pooled medians were 6.144 and 31.232 us, with 250 valid samples per arm. Repository dispatch_samples and derive_paired_timing independently replayed all 28 activity cohorts. This remains a local_serialized directional diagnostic with external GPU activity not excluded, not a registered Workload Evaluation or general performance qualification. A two-row FP64 variant compiled on both versions, but its only device attempt was refused as maca_broker_busy before any kernel call. At the clean current Compiler commit, an explicit Cake cast to fp64 is refused at the frontend because DType admits only bf16, fp16, fp32, fp8_e4m3 and int32. Thus there is no current Cake source for this internal precision route.
proposed_change: Do not add FP64 buffers or hide an FP64 accumulator inside the existing compensated contract from this diagnostic. First register the fixed FP8 matrix Workload with the independent high-precision reference and held-out finite distributions, seal both candidates under one exact C550 runtime, and repeat correctness plus paired MCPTI confirmation. If FP64 precision and latency remain necessary, decide whether an explicit reduction-accumulator precision contract or a fully typed FP64 DType is the smaller stable owner; carry construction typing, effects, dataflow, resource/cost analyses, backend emission and refusals, Corpus counterexamples, and the exact host/toolchain requirements in the same reviewed Compiler change. A new Target capability must be based on that route's device evidence, not on successful standalone compilation alone.
principles: P1/P3 require one canonical way to name internal reduction precision; P2 makes FP64 accumulation and timing implications visible; P4/P5/P7 require typing and every affected analysis with syntax; P6 checks positive and owned-refusal Corpus cases; P8 distinguishes compiled software lowering and bounded C550 numerics from an unobserved native FP64 instruction or broad hardware ceiling.

two_row_successor.observation: The first two-row FP64 device attempt remains maca_broker_busy with zero kernel calls. A create-only successor under the same C550-2 runtime matched all 20480 frozen words and the 4096-word plain-sum held-out failure matrix bitwise, with FP8 input bytes unchanged. A same-shape two-row FP64 versus two-row FP32 Neumaier diagnostic passed the predeclared MCPTI quality gate, 10/10 reversed pair wins and four A/A control ties: 250 samples per arm yielded pooled medians of 17.152 and 42.240 us, while A/A medians were both 42.240 us. All 28 raw cohorts were independently replayed through dispatch_samples and derive_paired_timing. This strengthens the case for an explicitly named internal-precision route on the already represented rank-two tile, but it is still a standalone local_serialized diagnostic without a registered Workload, sealed candidate or excluded external activity; it neither qualifies a general speedup nor proves a native FP64 instruction.

promotion_disposition: Keep this as a proposed capacity finding. The two-row successor avoids the one-row AccessMap shape gap in principle, but no Cake contract currently names FP64 internal accumulation. Review an explicit reduction-precision or instruction contract with its typing, resource/cost analyses and exact target admission only after a frozen Workload and formal paired qualification; do not silently replace the existing FP32-compensated implementation.
